problem_text:
A shipping company must devise a replenishment and storage strategy for its primary fuel reserve across a 20-week operational schedule.
The initial fuel reserve at the start of the planning window is 38 thousand liters.
In each week t = 1, ..., 20, the fuel supplier permits the company to schedule a delivery, the volume of which must fall between 3 and 48 thousand liters.
Crucially, every scheduled delivery requires a 2-week transit time before it becomes available for consumption or to augment the reserve.
The weekly fuel consumption requirement is specified as follows:
* Week 1: consumption 43 thousand liters
* Week 2: consumption 23 thousand liters
* Week 3: consumption 38 thousand liters
* Week 4: consumption 30 thousand liters
* Week 5: consumption 10 thousand liters
* Week 6: consumption 58 thousand liters
* Week 7: consumption 26 thousand liters
* Week 8: consumption 36 thousand liters
* Week 9: consumption 47 thousand liters
* Week 10: consumption 43 thousand liters
* Week 11: consumption 45 thousand liters
* Week 12: consumption 18 thousand liters
* Week 13: consumption 55 thousand liters
* Week 14: consumption 31 thousand liters
* Week 15: consumption 55 thousand liters
* Week 16: consumption 46 thousand liters
* Week 17: consumption 51 thousand liters
* Week 18: consumption 44 thousand liters
* Week 19: consumption 34 thousand liters
* Week 20: consumption 22 thousand liters

Supply shortfalls are permissible, but any unfulfilled consumption requirement is permanently lost and will not be carried forward.
Throughout the 20-week horizon, fuel volumes are treated as continuous quantities, and the total volume of fuel held in reserve at any point must not surpass the depot's capacity of 57 thousand liters.
The aggregate expenditure over the planning window comprises three elements: the procurement cost, amounting to 2 per thousand liters ordered; the storage cost, amounting to 3 per thousand liters of fuel held over from one week to the next; and the deficit penalty, amounting to 10 per thousand liters of unmet consumption. The objective is to establish the optimal delivery volume for each week and to monitor the consequent reserve levels and shortfalls in order to minimize the total expenditure.
